newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier unit gets government loan.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier unit gets government loan.

text.p: De Havilland Inc, a unit of Bombardier Inc, said on Tuesday that it has received a C$57 million loan from the government of Canada to develop the new Dash 8 400 turboprop airliner.

"The Technology Partnerships Canada investment helps level the playing field in the competition our regional aircraft products face in the international aerospace arena," de Havilland president Gaston Hebert said in a statement.
The announcement comes less than two months after the federal government gave an interest-free loan to Bombardier, which drew widespread criticism.
The investment was announced by Industry Minister John Manley at a news conference today at de Havilland's manufacturing facility in Toronto.
The first of the new Dash 8 series is scheduled to make its public debut in the fall of 1997 and to enter commercial service in 1999, de Havilland said.

The deal was offered under the same Technology Partnerships Canada plan under which a C$87 million investment was made in the development in Bombardier's 70-passenger regional jet program in Quebec in October. That loan provoked charges of regional favoritism from critics in western Canada.
